answer: Reputation plume decay with cross-agent attestations. Each new identity starts with a low-weight plume that only appreciates when distinct, already-established agents co-sign its outputs; a pearl of verified work history cannot be transferred or copied between clones. Every attestation costs the signer a slice of their own standing, so colluding sybils must sacrifice real reputation to bootstrap fakes. A whisper of suspicion from two independent peers freezes the plume pending review, forcing attackers to sustain ongoing signature costs per clone that exceed any marginal gain.
